clue.text: Musical some Parisian brought back is having soothing effect

indicators.note: brought back says the joined pieces are read from end to start

parts.note: Evita is the Lloyd Webber musical
des is French for 'some'

explanation.surface: A show with a bit of French flair is said to calm the nerves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' turns EVITADES round to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A sedative drug is one that calms, so as an adjective it describes something with a calming effect.

clue.text: Grotty old carriage parked outside B&B

indicators.note: outside says the carriage goes round the two letters

parts.note: a shay, or chaise, is an old light carriage
the two Bs of bed and breakfast

explanation.surface: A shabby old coach left in front of a guesthouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grotty' is British slang for grimy or unpleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: Grotty and shabby are near synonyms, both meaning run-down and in poor condition.

clue.text: Lunatic getting upset over request to provide material

indicators.note: over says the first piece sits above the second in this down answer
getting upset means overturned, so in a down clue the word reads upwards

parts.note: lunatic means mad
to ask is to request

explanation.surface: A madman throws a tantrum when asked to hand over some fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Damask is a patterned woven fabric, typically silk or linen.

clue.text: Wrong to get rude, somehow making one distressed

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law

indicators.note: somehow says the letters of rude are arranged in some other way

explanation.surface: Turning crude is somehow wrong and upsets someone.
explanation.walkthrough: A tort is a legal wrong; 'somehow' rearranges RUDE to URED.
explanation.definitionFit: Being tormented leaves a person in deep anguish, greatly upset.

clue.text: Fault with item in workshop

definitions.meaning: a moral failing or bad habit
a bench clamp that holds work steady

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a weakness of character and the gripping tool bolted to a workbench.

clue.text: SF film with US singer, one to impress

parts.note: E.T. is Spielberg's science-fiction film
Cher is the American singer

explanation.surface: A sci-fi movie featuring a pop diva, designed to wow audiences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'impress' here means press an image into a plate, not dazzle someone.
explanation.definitionFit: An etcher incises designs into metal plates, so the person makes impressions in a literal sense.

clue.text: Part of body with duty to store hard gold

indicators.note: to store means the duty holds the other pieces inside

parts.note: a tax is a duty
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A body part comes with a levy for keeping solid bullion.
explanation.definitionFit: The thorax is the chest region, between neck and abdomen.

clue.text: His anger comes out in judicial enquiries

indicators.note: comes out means the letters break out of their order and form anew

explanation.surface: A judge's temper shows during court sessions.
explanation.definitionFit: Courts hold sessions where evidence and argument are heard, so trials or tribunals.

clue.text: Eruption with head showing intemperance

parts.note: a rash is an eruption on the skin
a ness is a headland or promontory, as in place names on the coast

explanation.surface: An outburst with someone in charge showing lack of restraint.
explanation.walkthrough: NESS is a headland, a promontory; 'head' is the shortened sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Recklessness and intemperance both describe a lack of self-control or moderation.

clue.text: Member cares about dangerous situation escalating

parts.note: an arm is a member, a limb of the body

indicators.note: about here means scattered around, so the letters of cares are rearranged

explanation.surface: A club member worries over a deteriorating crisis.
explanation.definitionFit: Competing nations building ever more weapons make a perilous build-up, the classic Cold War rivalry.

clue.text: Homeless types with boy going round collecting nuts

indicators.note: collecting means the turned-round word gathers the other inside it
going round means the word for boy is turned to face the other way

parts.note: a son is a boy
nuts means crazy, mad

explanation.surface: Rough sleepers accompanied by a lad who wanders about gathering nuts.
explanation.definitionFit: Nomads are wanderers with no fixed abode, so they are people without a settled home.

clue.text: Part of university group girl is kept outside

indicators.note: is kept outside means the girl's name wraps round the group

parts.note: Fay is a girl's name
a cult is a sect, a group

explanation.surface: A sect at a college locks a young woman out.
explanation.definitionFit: A faculty is a division of a university, such as the arts or the sciences.

clue.text: European foundation opened by queen

indicators.note: opened by means the foundation word is split to take the other piece

parts.note: a base is a foundation

explanation.surface: A building's base is cut into by a monarch at a ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: A Basque is a native of the region straddling Spain and France, so a European.

clue.text: Biblical land penetrated by princess from place across the Pond

indicators.note: penetrated by means the land's name is entered by the princess

parts.note: Canaan is the Promised Land of the Bible
Di is Princess Diana

explanation.surface: The Promised Land invaded by a royal visitor from overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'across the Pond' means across the Atlantic, seen from Britain: North America.
explanation.definitionFit: Canada lies across the Atlantic from Britain, so its native or citizen is from there.

clue.text: Brightly coloured bird losing its tail

indicators.note: losing its tail means the last letter of the bird is cut off

parts.note: a flamingo is a pink wading bird

explanation.surface: A vivid bird that has lost its tail feathers.
explanation.definitionFit: Something flaming is fiery-hued, blazing red or orange.

clue.text: Very enthusiastic Greek god gets a look in

indicators.note: in says the short pieces go inside the god's name

parts.note: Zeus is king of the Greek gods
lo is an old word meaning look!

explanation.surface: An eager deity from Olympus manages to get a peek.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone zealous is full of fervour, eager to the point of fanaticism.

clue.text: Goes wild, losing head for a very long time

indicators.note: losing head means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: to rage is to go wild

explanation.surface: Someone goes berserk, losing their head for ever.
explanation.definitionFit: 'For ages' is an idiom for a long while, an eternity in casual speech.

clue.text: Endlessly applaud one in concert broadcast

indicators.note: in says these pieces go inside the concert word

parts.note: a Prom is a BBC Proms concert

indicators.note: Endlessly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to clap is to applaud
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Clapping endlessly at a televised concert.
explanation.walkthrough: The Proms are a British summer concert series.
explanation.definitionFit: To proclaim is to announce publicly, to spread news widely.

clue.text: Confession of mistake in football match may be related

parts.note: the ref is the referee, the official in a football match
erred is what one says in owning up to a mistake

explanation.surface: An official admits a howler at a soccer game.
explanation.walkthrough: Read together the clue's opening says a referee owned up to getting it wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Something referred to is mentioned or attributed, so connected or told.

clue.text: Shopkeeper given abuse about supply potentially drying up?

indicators.note: about means the abuse goes round the supply

parts.note: to jeer is to heap abuse
a well is a water supply that may run dry

explanation.surface: A retailer is taunted over goods that may run out.
explanation.definitionFit: A jeweller is a merchant who sells rings, necklaces and gems.

clue.text: Smell coming from Athens, maybe? Not good

indicators.note: Not says the letter for good is left out

parts.note: a person from Athens is an example of a Greek

explanation.surface: An unpleasant whiff from the Greek capital?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Athens' stands for an Athenian, so a Greek.
explanation.definitionFit: To reek is to stink, give off a strong offensive odour.

clue.text: English politician restricted, having nothing more to offer

parts.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament
tied means restricted, bound

explanation.surface: An English MP, bound by rules, has run out of ideas.
explanation.definitionFit: Something drained or exhausted of its contents has nothing left inside to give.

clue.text: Long pin, being distorted, ends in the litter

parts.note: skew means distorted, askew

indicators.note: ends in takes the final letters of the words the and litter

explanation.surface: A long spike, bent out of shape, finishes up among the rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: A skewer is a long metal or wooden spike for holding meat.

clue.text: Gum to chew not consumed

indicators.note: not says the word for consumed is removed

parts.note: to masticate is to chew
ate means consumed

explanation.surface: Gum to munch without swallowing.
explanation.definitionFit: Mastic is a resin from a Mediterranean tree, used as a gum and adhesive.

clue.text: Requirement for spectacles to be offered by game

definitions.meaning: the part of a pair of glasses resting on the nose
a card game for four players in pairs

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the nose-piece of glasses and the partnership card game.

clue.text: Making noise about a top man after second bit of scandal

indicators.note: after puts the rest following the letter taken from scandal
second bit of picks the second letter of the word scandal

parts.note: re means about, concerning
a king is the top man of a realm

explanation.surface: A fuss about a leading figure follows some juicy gossip.
explanation.definitionFit: Creaking is the squeaky grating sound of old timbers or hinges.

clue.text: Withdraw remedy

definitions.meaning: to retire or go off somewhere, as in withdrawing to the drawing room

explanation.definitionFit: One word means both go off somewhere, as in betaking oneself to bed, and mend what is broken.

clue.text: Some idiots ignore indicator

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some fools pay no attention to a warning sign.
explanation.definitionFit: A sign points something out or shows it, as a marker or pointer does.

clue.text: Indicators of ancient mounds truncated at the front

indicators.note: truncated at the front means the first letter is cut off

parts.note: barrows are prehistoric burial mounds

explanation.surface: Signs pointing to prehistoric earthworks with their fronts cut away.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrows are signs that point the way, so they show direction.

clue.text: William wanting summer in Paris had finally found accommodation

parts.note: Bill is short for William
ete is French for summer

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of the word had

explanation.surface: A man missing a French summer holiday had at last found somewhere to stay.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers billeted somewhere are lodged there, given a place to stay.

clue.text: New day in which revolutionary makes a comeback

indicators.note: in which says the day holds the other piece

parts.note: Mon is short for Monday

indicators.note: makes a comeback means the word goes back, read from right to left

parts.note: a Red is a communist revolutionary

explanation.surface: A fresh day on which a rebel returns to the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Modern means up to date, of recent times, the opposite of old.

clue.text: Interlude with silly utterances putting us off

indicators.note: silly says the letters of utterances are jumbled, once us is set aside

explanation.surface: A break in a show where foolish remarks put people off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting us off' takes U and S from UTTERANCES; 'silly' rearranges the remaining TTERANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: An entr'acte is an interval between acts of a play, or music played during it.
